api:
<StatusHistory> shows a grid of samples: one row per thing and one cell per sample, each cell coloured by its value. Use it when every sample matters: periodic health checks, hourly SLO results, a value per day. It is a port of Grafana's Status history panel; see Coming from Grafana.

use blenderui::prelude::*;
use bui_charts::*;

Status History shares its colours, value mappings, tooltip, legend and pages with State Timeline. Not sure which of the two you need? See the guide.

None, f64::NAN and StateValue::Null are missing values: their cells stay empty unless a mapping such as Special::Null names them.

How cells are drawn

  • One cell per sample. Each sample gets a column as wide as the typical gap between samples. The cell is centred on the sample's time, and col_width is how much of the column it fills. Equal neighbours never merge; use State Timeline for that.
  • Rows. Each row gets an equal share of the height; row_height is how much of it the cells fill.
  • Fill and outline. Cells are filled at fill_opacity, with a line_width outline in the full colour.
  • Value text is centred in the cell. Auto writes it when at least two characters fit, Always when one fits, Never hides it.
  • Tooltip. Hovering shows the sample's time and value. Tooltip::multi() lists every row at that sample.
  • Zooming. Drag across the cells to zoom the time axis; double-click to zoom out. on_select receives the range.

examples.title: Service checks
examples.description: Hourly checks, one cell per sample, renamed and coloured by mappings.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn service_checks() {
    let data = use_signal(probes(16));
    rsx! {
        <StatusHistory data={data} x={|p: &Probe| p.time} mappings={&*STATES} x_axis={time()} class="h-64">
            <StatusRow name="api" value={|p: &Probe| p.api} />
            <StatusRow name="web" value={|p: &Probe| p.web} />
            <StatusRow name="db" value={|p: &Probe| p.db} />
            <StatusRow name="cache" value={|p: &Probe| p.cache} />
        </StatusHistory>
    }
}

examples.title: Weekly grid
examples.description: Numeric x with a custom label format: busy hours per day.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn week() {
    let data = use_signal(
        Frame::new(["day", "00–06", "06–12", "12–18", "18–24"]).with_rows(
            (0..7u64)
                .map(|day| {
                    let busy = |slot: u64, base: f64| (base + noise(day * 4 + slot) * 30.).round();
                    [
                        day as f64,
                        busy(0, 5.),
                        busy(1, 45.),
                        busy(2, 60.),
                        busy(3, 30.),
                    ]
                })
                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        ),
    );
    rsx! {
        <StatusHistory
            data={data}
            color={GaugeColor::Scheme(Scheme::Oranges)}
            min={0.}
            max={90.}
            x_axis={AxisConfig::new().format(|day| ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"][(day as usize).min(6)].into())}
            class="h-56"
        />
    }
}

examples.title: Drag to zoom
examples.description: Drag across the cells; on_select reports the range.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn zoom() {
    let data = use_signal(probes(48));
    let picked = use_signal(SharedString::Borrowed(
        "Drag across the cells to zoom. Double-click to zoom out.",
    ));
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-56">
            <div class="text-xs">{picked.get()}</div>
            <StatusHistory
                data={data}
                x={|p: &Probe| p.time}
                mappings={&*STATES}
                show_value={VisibilityMode::Never}
                on_select={move |range: SelectedRange, _: &mut Window, _: &mut App| {
                    let hours = (range.x.1 - range.x.0) / HOUR;
                    picked.set(SharedString::from(format!("Zoomed to {hours:.0} hours")));
                }}
                x_axis={time()}
                class="flex-1"
            >
                <StatusRow name="api" value={|p: &Probe| p.api} />
                <StatusRow name="db" value={|p: &Probe| p.db} />
            </StatusHistory>
        </div>
    }
}
